study.title: Transcriptional profiling of livers from mice flown on Rodent Research Reference Mission-1 (RRRM-1)
study.study_scope: Animal spaceflight research; not direct astronaut health telemetry.
study.biological_context: Female BALB/cAnNTac mice; the study profiles liver tissue using ribodepleted total RNA sequencing.
study.mission_context: Rodent Research-8 on the International Space Station. The study includes ISS-terminal animals, live-animal-return animals, and matched ground, basal, and vivarium controls.
study.relevance: Provides spaceflight-associated biological research context for understanding how mission conditions can affect animal tissues.
sample_context: 160 mice were included across young and old cohorts and control groups.
The metadata reports 7-10 liver samples per group.
Young mice were 10-12 weeks old; old mice were 32 weeks old.
available_measurements: Illumina NovaSeq platform; paired-end 149 bp reads.
Public raw sequence, processed count, normalized count, and differential-expression files are listed by the study metadata.
study.availability_note: AstroHealth imports verified study metadata only. It does not download or transform RNA-seq measurements into astronaut telemetry.
study.license_note: The NASA OSDR AWS Open Data Registry entry states that the data has no restrictions on use. Cite NASA OSDR and the study accession.

additional_studies.title: Low dose (0.04 Gy) irradiation (LDR) and hindlimb unloading (HLU) microgravity in mice: brain transcriptomic and epigenomic data
additional_studies.study_scope: Animal ground research; not direct astronaut health telemetry.
additional_studies.biological_context: Mature, 6-month-old female C57BL/6 mice. Brain and eye-related tissues were collected after the modeled spaceflight conditions.
additional_studies.mission_context: This is a ground-based model for spaceflight, not an ISS mission. Hindlimb unloading models unloading, fluid shift, and physiological stress; whole-body 57Co gamma irradiation models a low-dose radiation component.
additional_studies.relevance: Its combined unloading and low-dose radiation design provides animal research context for studying biological responses relevant to spaceflight health, while not predicting human crew outcomes.
sample_context: Mice were hindlimb-suspended and/or irradiated for 21 days.
Tissues were collected 7 days and 1, 4, and 9 months after treatment.
The study was released as a NASA-funded ground study; it is not astronaut telemetry.
available_measurements: Brain transcriptomic profiling by RNA sequencing.
Transcription profiling by Illumina DNA microarray.
DNA methylation profiling by reduced-representation bisulfite sequencing.
additional_studies.availability_note: AstroHealth imports verified study metadata only. It does not download or transform OSD-202 measurements into astronaut telemetry.
additional_studies.license_note: The NASA OSDR AWS Open Data Registry entry states that the data has no restrictions on use. Cite NASA OSDR and the study accession.

payload.distinction: NASA research metadata and measurement availability are shown separately from AstroHealth's seeded simulated astronaut telemetry. The OSDR study does not calibrate the simulator, alerts, forecasts, readiness score, or medical conclusions.
